title: Multiquadratic fields and genus theory, Part II: real quadratic signs and form characters
summary: Extend the built multiquadratic and narrow genus theory by an explicit real quadratic kernel statement, descent of real class characters, exact cardinalities of genus fibres, and the arithmetic sign criteria used in real quadratic period formulas. Compare the imported form character with the existing ideal character at positive fundamental discriminants, keeping general form carriers and character well-definedness with Geometry of Numbers.
readme: This Part II starts from the built narrow class group, genus quotient and prime-discriminant character theory of Multiquadratic. Its exact conventions, theorem inventory, acceptance examples and supplier contracts are documented in research/blueprint/readmes/MultiquadraticPartII.md. The finite genus and sign adapters lead to the fundamental form/ideal comparison. General form theory is imported, and no class-number-one infinitude or analytic equidistribution theorem is asserted.

stages.title: The real quadratic narrow defect
stages.description: Fix a number field K generated by an integral θ with minimal polynomial X²−d, d>0 squarefree, and D=fundamentalDiscriminant(d)>1. Use the existing narrow class group C=Cl⁺(K), forgetful map π:C→Cl(K), and J=mkPrincipal(θ). Import J²=1 and the norm −1 unit criterion. Export the exact set identity ker(π)={1,J} and, for each real character χ:C→{±1}, existence and uniqueness of a character ψ:Cl(K)→{±1} with ψ∘π=χ exactly when χ(J)=1. The quotient statement Cl(K)≅C/⟨J⟩ uses the existing first isomorphism theorem; no new quotient carrier is built.

stages.title: Equal cardinalities of narrow genera
stages.description: A genus is a class in the existing elementary-two quotient C/C², not an element of C[2]. For every g∈C/C² let G_g={A∈C:q(A)=g}. With r=ω(D)=the number of rational primes ramified in K, prove 2^(r−1)|G_g|=h⁺(D), where h⁺(D)=|C|. Obtain equal, nonempty finite fibres and the rational formula |G_g|=2^(1−r)h⁺(D) from this identity and the imported rank theorem. Use existing coset equivalences; no duplicate genus or fibre construction is introduced.

stages.title: Signs of genus characters
stages.description: Let s be the prime-discriminant factorization of positive D and t⊆s, with δ=∏t and δ′=∏(s\t); the empty product 1 is permitted. Extend the imported singleton sign formula to χ_t(J)=sign(δ)=sign(δ′). Prove that every P∈s is positive exactly when no rational prime p≡3 modulo4 divides D. For positive fundamental D, prove that the latter condition is equivalent to D=x²+y² with x,y integers. Combine these adapters with the built principal genus theorem to obtain J∈C² exactly under either arithmetic condition, equivalently every genus character is even on J. If a prime p≡3 modulo4 divides D, deduce J≠1 and that no integral unit has norm −1. This direction is sufficient, not necessary; membership J∈C² is weaker than J=1.

stages.title: Fundamental form and ideal characters
stages.description: Import the integral binary form character from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.2 and the oriented primitive-form/narrow-ideal dictionary from GN.3. For positive fundamental D, t⊆s and primitive Q=[a,b,c] with discriminant D representing the narrow class A in the DIT16 convention, prove χ_δ(Q)=χ_t(A). The proof uses a positive integer m represented by Q and coprime to δ, together with a nonzero integral ideal of absolute norm m in A⁻¹. Explain the coefficient changes [a,−b,c]↔A⁻¹, [−a,b,−c]↔JA and −Q↔JA⁻¹. Their character consequences follow from this comparison and RQ.2; the dictionary itself remains supplied by GN.3. Imprimitive and nonfundamental form characters, reduction algorithms and analytic periods stay with their owners.
